page.layout: One printed page (left-hand page of the opening is not shown; this is the right page). One text column with small-type marginal references in the left and right margins; below the text a rule, a centred heading "INGENII," with a sub-line, and a closing paragraph with a dropped initial and a catchword-like name at the right. Running head at top; page number at top left.

p.i: Risus eram positus inter convivia mensis.

main_text.p: Iniuriarum & offensionum semper est memoria: beneficiorumrum non item.
Stultus est, qui illi male aegre patitur dici, qui facit.
Iniuria etiam rebus inanimatis inferri potest.

p.i: Quia est, qui tam protervè nostris foribus facit injuriam?

main_text.p: Vim facere in oppido pacato, & quidem luce, in via, & libero homini, nefas.
In eos à quibus accepimus beneficia, non debemus esse injurij.
Graeci moris fuit, ad vim, injuriamq; arcendam, confugere ad templa, statuas, aras.
main_text.head: INGENII,
main_text.p: Ingenii hebetudinem arguit crassities cutis. Unde de homine stupido dicitur Mil. 2. 2, v. 80.

page.notes: Marginal notes and the mark-up of the Plautus references are partly uncertain; the left-hand page is not on this scan. Some marginal text at the far right edge is cut off by the binding and is not transcribed. The printed line "Iniuriarum ... beneficio-rum non item" is hyphenated across lines.
